The cited sentence explains the motivation for using strings (to avoid binary float precision errors) and provides "2.675" as an example of a value that is problematic for floats. It does not specify the exact rounding behavior (e.g., round half up vs. round half to even) or mandate that every specific halfway value in the 2.6-3.0 range must round to a specific target string. The test asserts specific outcomes for many values that go beyond the general requirement to preserve precision, effectively enforcing a specific rounding algorithm not explicitly required by the text.
